title: The SEO Funnel: Map Content to TOFU, MOFU, BOFU September 2026
summary: Build an SEO funnel that covers every stage of the buyer journey. Learn keyword mapping, internal linking, and BOFU conversion tactics. September 2026
body_markdown:
Most SEO content strategies are accidentally one-stage operations. Teams build out the educational top-of-funnel content, get the traffic, and then lose the buyer the moment they start comparing options because the middle of the funnel is thin or missing entirely. Getting all three stages right (and connecting them) is where the actual revenue from organic search comes from. Here's how to build that out.


**TLDR:**


- An SEO funnel maps keywords and content to TOFU, MOFU, and BOFU stages so your site shows up at every point in the buyer journey.
- Only 4% of visitors are ready to buy on a first visit, so publishing only bottom-funnel content makes you invisible to 96% of potential buyers.
- BOFU traffic converts at a significantly higher rate than TOFU traffic, but 68% of B2B deals stall at MOFU because most teams leave the middle stage thin.
- AI Overviews carry a high zero-click rate (published estimates vary widely by query type and study), so treat TOFU as a citation-building exercise and put your conversion logic in MOFU and BOFU pages.
- Maintouch runs the full SEO funnel as one continuous system, including zero-volume query mining, automated internal linking, and citation tracking across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, and Claude.


## What Is an SEO Funnel?


An SEO funnel is the path a buyer takes from their first search query to becoming a customer, guided at every step by organic content. It's the search-specific version of a broader marketing funnel: instead of mapping ads, emails, and events, you're mapping keywords and content to where someone is in their decision process.


The general marketing funnel tracks all channels. The SEO funnel tracks one: search. And increasingly, that means both Google results and AI-generated answers in tools like ChatGPT and Perplexity.


Get the funnel right, and your content shows up when buyers need it most.


## How the SEO Funnel Differs from a Sales Funnel


A sales funnel spans every channel: paid ads, email sequences, cold outreach, events. The SEO funnel covers one channel only: organic search. Same stages, different levers.


Where a sales funnel uses ad spend and outbound cadences to move buyers forward, the SEO funnel uses keywords, content, and internal links. You're not pushing buyers through a sequence. You're publishing content that meets them at each search they run naturally.


The stages map identically. What changes is the mechanic.


## The Three Stages of the SEO Funnel: TOFU, MOFU, and BOFU


Every SEO funnel runs through three stages, each matching a different buyer mindset.[Only 4% of website visitors](https://content-whale.com/blog/your-guide-to-tofu-mofu-bofu-marketing-strategy/) are ready to buy on a first visit, which means if you're only publishing bottom-funnel content, you're invisible to 96% of your potential buyers.


Stage Buyer State Content Goal


TOFU (Top of Funnel) Problem-aware, not solution-aware Build awareness, earn trust


MOFU (Middle of Funnel) Weighing options Educate, set apart


BOFU (Bottom of Funnel) Ready to decide Convert


The stages aren't arbitrary. A buyer searching "what is programmatic SEO" needs something completely different than one searching "[best programmatic SEO tool](https://maintouch.com/blogs/best-programmatic-seo-tools-scaling-content) ." Same buyer, different moment, different content requirement.


## Top of Funnel (TOFU): Building Awareness Through Informational Content


TOFU content targets buyers who don't know you exist yet. They're searching broad informational queries: "what is technical SEO," "how does content marketing work," "why does my site rank poorly." Blog posts, how-to guides, and educational explainers are the formats that capture this traffic.


The job here is awareness, not conversion. In[B2B SEO marketing](https://maintouch.com/blogs/b2b-seo-strategy-and-tactics) , buyers complete an[estimated 57%](https://beanstalkim.com/learn/seo/tofu-vs-bofu/) of their purchase evaluation before ever speaking to a sales rep, so TOFU content is doing real buying-process work even when it doesn't look like it. A buyer who reads your "what is programmatic SEO" guide today may not convert for six months, but you're already in their consideration set.


Resist the urge to push product at this stage. The reader isn't ready, and a sales pitch here burns the trust you just built.


## Middle of Funnel (MOFU): Nurturing Leads with Consideration Content


MOFU is where buyers compare. They're searching "best SEO tool for SaaS," "\[competitor\] vs \[competitor\]," and "alternatives to \[tool they're currently using\]." Comparison guides, "best of" listicles, use-case solution pages, and detailed feature breakdowns are the formats that capture this intent.


It's also the most underfunded stage. 68% of B2B deals stall at consideration because most teams pour budget into awareness content and bottom-funnel conversion pages, then leave the middle thin. The buyer shows up ready to weigh their choices and finds nothing.


That's where you lose the deal, not at the close.


## Bottom of Funnel (BOFU): Converting High-Intent Searchers


At BOFU, intent is explicit. Buyers are searching "\[your brand\] pricing," "\[your brand\] vs \[competitor\]," "best \[tool category\] demo," or "\[specific product\] for \[use case\]." Search volume is lower, but the buyer is ready to decide.


The content formats that win here:


- Pricing pages with clear plan breakdowns that answer the "what do I actually get" question without making the buyer dig
- Demo or trial request pages that remove friction at the exact moment someone is ready to act
- Head-to-head competitor comparison pages that give buyers the specifics they're already looking for
- Testimonial and case study pages that confirm others have made this call and it worked
- Product-specific landing pages tied to a use case, so the buyer sees their exact situation reflected back


BOFU traffic converts at a far higher rate than TOFU traffic. A buyer landing on your pricing page after reading a comparison guide isn't browsing. They want to confirm you're the right call before they reach out.


Design these pages for the buyer who's already sold on the category. They don't need education. They need specifics: what's included, what it costs, and why you over the alternative.


## How to Map Keywords to Each Funnel Stage


Keyword intent mapping is tagging each keyword with what the searcher actually wants, then assigning it to the right page and funnel stage. The four intent types are:


- Informational (learning something)
- Commercial (comparing options)
- Transactional (ready to act)
- Navigational (looking for a specific brand or page)


A[keyword competitor analysis](https://maintouch.com/blogs/seo-keyword-competitor-analysis) can help you identify which intent types your rivals are targeting and where you have gaps.


The fastest way to verify intent: run the query and read the SERP. If Google surfaces listicles and comparison guides, it's commercial. If it surfaces how-to posts and definitions, it's informational. Automated tools guess at intent from click data. The SERP shows you what Google has already decided.


One warning worth naming: a keyword can be correctly staged and still produce zero conversions if the page asks for more commitment than the searcher is ready to give. A TOFU reader landing on a pricing page bounces. A BOFU buyer landing on a 2,000-word explainer loses patience. Staging the keyword correctly is step one. Matching the page's offer to that stage is what closes the loop.


## How to Use Internal Linking to Move Buyers Through the Funnel


Internal links are the connective tissue between funnel stages. Without them, a buyer reads your TOFU post, learns something useful, and leaves. You got the traffic. You didn't move them anywhere.


The pattern is straightforward: educational posts link to comparison guides, comparison guides link to pricing or demo pages. Each piece of content should point toward the next logical question the buyer has. If someone's reading your "what is programmatic SEO" post, they're about to wonder which tools do it well. Link them there before they go back to Google. An[SEO checklist for technical and content tasks](https://maintouch.com/blogs/seo-checklist-automation-shortcuts) helps make certain these linking opportunities are never missed.


The highest-impact move most teams skip: linking from[high-traffic TOFU pages](https://www.getpassionfruit.com/blog/how-to-map-content-to-every-stage-of-the-buyer-s-journey-seo-funnel-strategy) to the right MOFU pages. A single well-placed internal link on a post getting 5,000 monthly visitors drives more qualified MOFU traffic than publishing three more top-of-funnel articles. The audience is already there. Point them forward.


Most teams have the TOFU, the MOFU, and the BOFU sitting in complete isolation. The funnel exists on paper and nowhere else.


## How AI Search and Zero-Click Results Are Reshaping the Funnel


The funnel still works. It's just shifting where the value lives.


[AI Overviews 83% zero-click rate](https://click-vision.com/zero-click-search-statistics) , meaning most informational queries never send a visitor anywhere. Traditional queries aren't far behind,[averaging around 60% zero-click](https://www.workshopdigital.com/blog/rise-in-zero-click-searches-deep-dive/) . For TOFU content, that's a structural change in how value gets delivered.


Informational content still matters, but the return is brand visibility, not traffic. A buyer who sees your brand cited in a ChatGPT answer about "what is programmatic SEO" didn't visit your site. But they registered the name. This is the core premise of[answer engine optimization](https://maintouch.com/blogs/what-is-answer-engine-optimization-complete-guide) : earning visibility in AI-generated responses even without a click. When they move to MOFU and start comparing tools, you're already in their frame.


MOFU and BOFU content is where clicks still happen consistently. Commercial and transactional queries ("best SEO tool for SaaS," "Maintouch pricing") carry enough decision weight that buyers click through to verify. That's where your organic traffic conversion logic should live now.


The practical adjustment: treat TOFU as a citation-building exercise, not a traffic play. Structure informational content in passage-level blocks that[Google AI Overviews](https://maintouch.com/blogs/ai-overview-aio-seo-impact) and other AI engines can pull directly, then invest proportionally more in MOFU and BOFU pages where the click still follows the search.


## Common SEO Funnel Mistakes and How to Fix Them


Five mistakes account for most broken SEO funnels.


- Publishing only TOFU content: traffic without conversion infrastructure is just an audience you can't monetize. If your top 10 posts are all educational and none link to a comparison page or pricing page, you have awareness with no path forward.
- Missing internal links between stages: a TOFU post with no link to a MOFU page is a dead end. The buyer leaves instead of moving forward.
- Mismatched CTAs: a "Start Free Trial" button on a definitional blog post asks for commitment the reader isn't ready to give. Match the ask to the stage. TOFU gets newsletter signups or related reads, MOFU gets demo requests or comparison guides, BOFU gets the direct conversion action.
- Ignoring low-volume BOFU pages: teams optimize for traffic volume and overlook "\[your brand\] vs \[competitor\]" pages sitting at 200 monthly searches. Those 200 searchers are ready to buy.
- Treating the funnel as linear: buyers move backward. Someone on a pricing page might click into a comparison guide to double-check their reasoning. Build for that recursion. BOFU pages should link back to MOFU content that handles objections, and not merely forward to a checkout.


Quick audit: pull your top 20 organic pages from Search Console. Tag each as TOFU, MOFU, or BOFU by intent. A structured[content audit to improve rankings](https://maintouch.com/blogs/run-content-audit-rankings) can surface exactly these gaps. Check whether each page has at least one internal link pointing to the next stage, and whether the CTA matches where the buyer is. Most teams find the same pattern: TOFU heavy, MOFU thin, BOFU almost nonexistent.


## How to Measure SEO Funnel Performance by Stage


Each stage needs different metrics. Applying the same measurement logic across all three is how good TOFU content gets killed in quarterly reviews.


- TOFU: impressions, organic sessions, and assisted conversions, not last-click revenue. Getting[cited in AI Overviews](https://maintouch.com/blogs/how-to-get-cited-in-ai-overviews) is another TOFU metric worth tracking, since AI citations build brand recall without generating a direct click. A post that touched 800 buyers before they converted doesn't show up in last-click attribution, so stakeholders defund it. That's a measurement problem, not a content problem.
- MOFU: demo requests, trial signups, and content-assisted MQLs. Track which comparison pages appear in the conversion path, and not merely which page gets the final click.
- BOFU: conversion rate by landing page, pipeline sourced by entry URL, and closed revenue traced back to organic entry point. Tracking[AI visibility metrics and KPIs](https://maintouch.com/blogs/ai-visibility-kpis-track-results) adds a fourth layer that captures influence from AI-generated answers.


The B2B buyer journey can stretch well past six months from first touch to a closed deal. Last-click attribution erases most of that runway. If you're reporting SEO performance to stakeholders using only last-click data, you're making your TOFU investment look worthless and your BOFU pages look like the only thing that matters.

### What is the relationship between SEO and AEO, and how much do they overlap?


They share the same foundation: AI engines like ChatGPT and Perplexity run a web search before generating answers, so strong Google rankings directly feed your citation rate in AI-generated responses. The difference is measurement and structure. SEO performance shows up in Search Console impressions and organic sessions, while AEO performance shows up in citation share across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, and Claude. You don't run two separate strategies; you run one content operation and score it against both scoreboards.


### Should I focus on Google SEO or AI search optimization first when starting from zero?


Start with Google SEO. AI engines pull from indexed pages, so if Google can't find and rank your content, AI tools won't cite it either. Build your foundational pages first, get them indexed and ranking, then layer in passage-level structuring and schema markup to become citation-eligible in AI-generated answers. The two aren't in competition; your SEO work is what makes AEO possible.
